title: Take a Prius radiator support cover off its three push clips, lifting each centre pin before its clip comes out
instruction: Take the radiator support opening cover off and lay it on the fender cover, so the front bumper can come off next. The three clips will be refitted, so keep them undamaged and put them in the parts tray.
context: Automotive service technicians (about 800,000 US workers) and body repairers (about 160,000, O*NET 49-3021: "Remove ... trim to gain access to vehicle bodies") unclip plastic covers on most front-end jobs. Toyota's 2010 Prius manual starts bumper removal with this cover: "Remove the 3 clips", then disengage 2 claws. A two-piece clip unlocks only once its centre pin is pried up; levering the body first snaps its legs.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the bumper top the robot works over. Fixed, the front of a 2010-2015 Toyota Prius engine bay, hood open: a blue fender cover (2 thick) over the bumper top from x 10 to 260, y -550 to 550; the chrome grille top, x 262-288, 32 high; the upper radiator support, black e-coated steel, x 290-420, top 40 up, 1,240 wide, with 8 mm square holes under the clips and 18 x 30 claw pockets at y +-300 (x 304-322); the hood latch, 67 x 70 x 45, on the support at x 328-395, y -35 to 35; clear headlamp tops, x 200-450, y +-470 to 620, 60 up; the radiator top behind, x 440-560, y -400 to 400, 25 up. On the support: the radiator support opening cover (Toyota 53289-47010, textured black polypropylene; 110 x 900 x 2.5, 0.35 kg, estimate), x 300-410, with a 90 mm notch round the latch, a 12 x 10 stiffening rib along its front edge (x 307.5-319.5) and two claws (20 wide, 9 deep, 4 mm hooks) at y +-300 hooked under the support's front edge. Three two-piece black nylon push clips (Toyota type, 7 mm hole size) hold it at x 355, y +230, +80 and -200 (estimate): 20 mm head 1.6 thick, 6.5 mm shank 13 long, a dark-grey centre pin with a 10 mm head 1.4 thick standing on a 4 mm neck 2.5 mm above the clip head, pin down (locked). Loose on the fender cover: a grey plastic parts tray, 90 x 240 x 20, 3 mm walls, 0.2 kg, centred at (95, 0); two Lisle 35460 double-ended clip lifters (203 long, zinc-plated steel with an 89 mm red vinyl grip, 80 g; narrow fork with a 5 mm opening for the pin, wide fork 10 mm for the clip body, 1.5 mm thick tines 12 long, ends straight and flush with the grip's underside; end shapes estimated) lying flat along y at (130, 370) and (130, -370), narrow ends toward the middle. Lot B: tray at (105, 30), lifters at (150, 395) and (115, -345); everything else as lot A. Real trial: on the car itself, or on a used upper radiator support section bolted level on a bench 40 mm above a board standing in for the bumper top, with the hood latch on it and a 32 mm strip in front for the grille top, at the places above. Trials alternate A, B and are averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read from the overhead video and a front video with a millimetre scale card behind the clip row, stepped frame by frame, a photo of the clips and tray after the trial (10x loupe for the clip legs) and a steel rule. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment: a clip body rises 2 mm or more before its centre pin has first come 4 mm up (on video against the scale; afterwards a snapped or stress-whitened leg in the photo); the cover is lifted 5 mm or more at a clip whose pin has not yet come 4 mm up (hole torn or clip pulled through); or anything drops more than 10 mm below the bumper top (off the car). Otherwise 0.2 for each clip in the parts tray: centre inside the walls, lowest point on the tray floor (within 4 mm), tray tilted under 18 degrees, no gripper within 5 mm and no lifter within 2 mm of it, moving under 20 mm/s: up to 0.6. 0.8: all three in the tray and the cover off, wholly at least 2 mm in front of the support's front edge and lying on the fender cover (lowest point within 15 mm of it), no gripper within 5 mm of it, moving under 20 mm/s. 1.0: that, with both grippers at least 30 mm from the cover, clips, lifters and tray and every one of them moving under 1 mm for 1 s. Any tool or the fingers may be used. Trials on lots A and B are averaged.
run_limit: 1,800 steps (90 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B), averaged
reset_notes: 1. Push the cover's claws under the support's front edge at y +-300 and lay the cover on the support. 2. Push a clip body into each of the three holes until its head is flat on the cover, then press its centre pin down until it clicks (its head 2.5 mm above the clip head). Replace any clip whose legs are damaged. 3. Set the tray and the two lifters at the lot's places (A: tray (95, 0), lifters (130, +-370); B: tray (105, 30), lifters (150, 395) and (115, -345)), lifters flat along y, narrow ends toward the middle. 4. Photograph the clips' legs after each trial.
fidelity: True-size cover and clips; cover size and mass, clip places, lifter end shapes (grip a 20 mm square) and all forces are estimates. Declared latch: a clip body is held down with 25 N until its pin first reaches 4 mm (0.8 N detent, estimate), then drags out against 1 N; the unlocked pin is pushed to its 6 mm stop. Legs do not collide. Holes are 8 mm square for 6.5 mm shanks, the support plate 3 mm (real 1.4). Clip parts weigh 10 g and 6 g (real 2 g).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lots A and B 0.0 each; both ran to the 1,800-step limit without refusing); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (all three clips lifted pin first into the tray, cover laid on the fender cover; full score at 73.5 s)
